dedupe_keys.name: us inland waterways vessel density ais derived 2015 to 2023

description: These map services show the density of vessel positions on US inland waterways for each year from 2015 to 2023, computed from Automatic Identification System (AIS) messages of US-registered commercial vessels in 5 m grid cells, with separate upstream and downstream density layers at 10 m for 2019. Only messages with speed over ground above 0.1 knots are counted, and the directional layers keep messages whose course lies within 60 degrees of the sailing line direction. The data come from the US Coast Guard National AIS database and from AIS stations of the US Army Corps of Engineers at inland facilities recorded in its Lock Operations Management Application; the USACE Inland Electronic Navigation Chart program worked with the Coast Guard to extract inland AIS data on location, time, ship type, speed, length, beam and draught. Coverage is the US inland waterway system. Access: free ArcGIS tiled map services, marked for public use, updated in 2024. Caveats: densities show relative intensity, not vessel counts, and only messages that were received and logged are included. It supports inland waterway traffic and capacity analysis, exposure of vessel traffic to low water and floods, and lock and channel disruption studies, and complements the USACE National Waterway Network and lock records catalogued here.
